    AI Overview

    AI Mode replied:

    To remove a fresh red wine stain, blot the excess liquid with a clean white cloth, cover the spot generously with salt to absorb the moisture, and rinse or wash with cool water. 
    General Rules for Wine Stains
    • Act fast: Treat the spill immediately.
    • Blot, do not rub: Rubbing pushes the pigment deeper into the fibers.
    • Use cold water: Hot water sets the tannins and makes the stain permanent.
    • Avoid heat: Never put stained clothes in the dryer until the stain is completely gone. 
    Methods by Material
    Clothes and Linens
    • Salt and Boiling Water:
      Cover the fresh stain with a thick layer of salt. Pour boiling water carefully over the stain from about a foot above, then wash in the washing machine.
       
    • Hydrogen Peroxide and Dish Soap: Mix two parts hydrogen peroxide with one part dish soap. Blot it on the stain, let it sit for 15 minutes, and rinse with cold water. 
    • Commercial Removers: Apply an enzymatic spray or a specialized product like OxiClean before washing. 
    Carpets and Rugs
    • Salt Absorption: Blot the wet spill, cover it liberally with salt, and let it sit for a few hours before vacuuming.
    • Soap and Peroxide: Dab the area with a mixture of dish soap and hydrogen peroxide, then blot dry with a clean cloth. 
    Couches and Upholstery
    • Baking Soda and Vinegar: Cover the damp stain with baking soda, spritz with white vinegar, let it bubble and dry, then vacuum the residue.
    • Check labels: Always test a hidden spot first to make sure the fabric is safe. 
    Watch a helpful demonstration on how to use salt and boiling water to lift a red wine stain:

    People also ask
    Can you get out a red wine stain after it's dried?
    AI Overview

    AI Mode replied:

    Yes, you can remove a red wine stain even after it has dried, though it takes a bit more work than a fresh spill. 
    Steps for Clothing and Fabrics
    • Soak in vinegar: Apply cleaning vinegar or white vinegar directly to the dried stain. Let it sit for at least one hour to break down the wine's tannins. 
    • Use oxygen bleach: Mix a powdered oxygen cleaner like OxiClean with hot water, or apply a mixture of three parts hydrogen peroxide and one part dish soap. 
    • Let it sit: Allow the cleaning mixture to rest on the stain for 20 to 60 minutes. 
    • Launder safely: Wash the item in the washing machine using cool or warm water. Check that the stain is completely gone before putting the item in the dryer, as heat will permanently set any remaining color. 
    Steps for Carpets and Couches
    • Dampen the area: Lightly dab the dried spot with cold water to loosen the old residue without soaking the backing material.
    • Mix a cleaning solution: Combine one tablespoon of dish soap, one tablespoon of white vinegar, and two cups of warm water.
    • Blot the stain: Sponge the solution onto the spot with a clean cloth, working from the outside edges inward to prevent spreading.
    • Rinse and dry: Blot with a clean, damp cloth to remove soap residue, then press a dry towel onto the area to absorb excess moisture.
